JavaScript · Polyfills

Write a polyfill for bind().

Answer

bind returns a new function that calls the original with a fixed this, the preset arguments, and any arguments passed later:

Function.prototype.myBind = function (context, ...preset) {
  if (typeof this !== 'function') throw new TypeError('myBind must be called on a function');
  const fn = this;
  return function bound(...later) {
    // With `new`, ignore the bound this, like native bind does.
    if (new.target) return new fn(...preset, ...later);
    return fn.apply(context, [...preset, ...later]);
  };
};

const user = { name: 'Sam' };
function greet(greeting, punct) { return `${greeting}, ${this.name}${punct}`; }
const hi = greet.myBind(user, 'Hi');
hi('!');                     // "Hi, Sam!"
hi.call({ name: 'X' }, '?'); // "Hi, Sam?" – this stays bound

Points to mention:

  • Partial application: preset arguments come first, later ones are appended.
  • The returned function is a closure over fn, context and preset.
  • new support is the usual follow-up: a bound function used as a constructor ignores the bound this.
  • If asked not to use apply, call the original through the myCall polyfill instead.
